verses.after: The governor told them not to eat any of the most holy food until a priest could serve with the Urim and Thummim.
verses.tsw_comparator: The governor told them that they should not eat from the most holy things until a priest stood with Urim and Thummim.

verses.rationale: Retains the stated overall count without adjusting it to the itemized figures.
verses.before: The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,
verses.after: The whole assembly numbered 42,360,
verses.tsw_comparator: The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,

verses.rationale: Makes enslavement and both gender distinctions explicit and keeps the additional singers separate.
verses.before: besides their male servants and female servants, who numbered seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven. They also had two hundred male and female singers.
verses.after: besides their 7,337 male and female slaves. They also had 200 male and female singers.
verses.tsw_comparator: besides their male servants and female servants, who numbered seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven. They also had two hundred male and female singers.

verses.rationale: Preserves both animal categories and their exact counts across the sentence.
verses.before: Their horses were seven hundred thirty-six; their mules, two hundred forty-five;
verses.after: They had 736 horses and 245 mules,
verses.tsw_comparator: Their horses were seven hundred thirty-six; their mules, two hundred forty-five;

verses.rationale: Completes the animal inventory without rounding the totals.
verses.before: their camels, four hundred thirty-five; their donkeys, six thousand seven hundred twenty.
verses.after: 435 camels and 6,720 donkeys.
verses.tsw_comparator: their camels, four hundred thirty-five; their donkeys, six thousand seven hundred twenty.

verses.rationale: Retains some leaders and the original site, connecting giving to rebuilding.
verses.before: When some of the heads of ancestral houses came to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, they gave freely for the house of God, to raise it on its site.
verses.after: When they reached the LORD’s house in Jerusalem, some of the family heads gave voluntary offerings for God’s house, to rebuild it on its site.
verses.tsw_comparator: When some of the heads of ancestral houses came to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, they gave freely for the house of God, to raise it on its site.

verses.rationale: Preserves the capacity-based giving, ancient units, and all amounts; units are explained separately.
verses.before: According to their ability they gave to the treasury for the work sixty-one thousand darics of gold, five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priestly garments.
verses.after: They gave as much as they could to the building fund: 61,000 gold darics, 5,000 silver minas, and 100 priestly robes.
verses.tsw_comparator: According to their ability they gave to the treasury for the work sixty-one thousand darics of gold, five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priestly garments.

verses.rationale: Retains the partial people phrase and the concluding repetition rather than merging the two statements.
verses.before: So the priests, the Levites, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants lived in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.
verses.after: The priests, Levites, some of the people, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants settled in their towns. All Israel was settled in its towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the priests, the Levites, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants lived in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.

verses.rationale: Preserves the timing and the united gathering after dispersal among towns.
verses.before: When the seventh month came and the children of Israel were in the cities, the people gathered as one in Jerusalem.
verses.after: When the seventh month arrived, the Israelites were in their towns. The people gathered as one in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the seventh month came and the children of Israel were in the cities, the people gathered as one in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Makes the two leadership groups readable and retains the authority and purpose of rebuilding.
verses.before: Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers the priests arose, along with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his brothers, and they built the altar of the God of Israel to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the instruction of Moses, the man of God.
verses.after: Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests, together with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his relatives, began rebuilding the altar of the God of Israel. They would offer burnt offerings on it, as written in the instruction of Moses, the man of God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers the priests arose, along with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his brothers, and they built the altar of the God of Israel to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the instruction of Moses, the man of God.

verses.rationale: Retains the causal wording linking fear and altar building and follows the read plural offered.
verses.before: They set the altar on its foundation despite their fear of the peoples of the lands, and they offered burnt offerings upon it to the LORD, burnt offerings morning and evening.
verses.after: They set the altar on its foundations, for they were afraid of the peoples of the surrounding lands. On it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD, morning and evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set the altar on its foundation despite their fear of the peoples of the lands, and they offered burnt offerings upon it to the LORD, burnt offerings morning and evening.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated daily rhythm and prescribed numbers without inventing them here.
verses.before: They kept the Festival of Booths as it is written and offered the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the ordinance for each day,
verses.after: They observed the Festival of Shelters as written, offering the required number of burnt offerings day by day, each day’s offerings according to its rule.
verses.tsw_comparator: They kept the Festival of Booths as it is written and offered the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the ordinance for each day,

verses.rationale: Keeps the four offering contexts distinct and does not merge voluntary giving into required sacrifice.
verses.before: and afterward the continual burnt offering, the offerings for the new moons and for all the appointed festivals of the LORD that were consecrated, and the offerings of everyone who freely offered a freewill offering to the LORD.
verses.after: After that came the regular burnt offerings, those for the new moons and all the LORD’s appointed holy festivals, and the offerings of everyone who gave a voluntary gift to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: and afterward the continual burnt offering, the offerings for the new moons and for all the appointed festivals of the LORD that were consecrated, and the offerings of everyone who freely offered a freewill offering to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the precise day and the distinction between restored altar worship and an unbuilt temple.
verses.before: From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, although the foundation of the temple of the LORD had not yet been laid.
verses.after: They began offering burnt offerings to the LORD on the first day of the seventh month, although the foundation of the LORD’s temple had not yet been laid.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, although the foundation of the temple of the LORD had not yet been laid.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two payment forms, transport route, and royal authorization.
verses.before: They gave silver to the masons and carpenters, and food, drink, and oil to the Sidonians and Tyrians to bring cedar logs from Lebanon by sea to Joppa, according to the authorization they had received from Cyrus king of Persia.
verses.after: They paid the stonecutters and craftsmen in silver. They gave food, drink, and oil to the Sidonians and Tyrians to bring cedar timber from Lebanon by sea to Joppa, under the authorization Cyrus king of Persia had granted them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They gave silver to the masons and carpenters, and food, drink, and oil to the Sidonians and Tyrians to bring cedar logs from Lebanon by sea to Joppa, according to the authorization they had received from Cyrus king of Persia.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the long sentence while retaining the exact date, all participants, and the oversight age.
verses.before: In the second year after they came to the house of God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak, the rest of their brothers the priests and Levites, and everyone who had come to Jerusalem from captivity began the work. They appointed the Levites from twenty years old and upward to oversee the work of the house of the LORD.
verses.after: In the second month of the second year after their arrival at God’s house in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak, and the rest of their fellow priests and Levites, with everyone who had returned to Jerusalem from captivity, began the work. They appointed Levites twenty years old and above to oversee the work on the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the second year after they came to the house of God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak, the rest of their brothers the priests and Levites, and all who had come to Jerusalem from captivity began the work. They appointed the Levites from twenty years old and upward to oversee the work of the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult Judah designation and all oversight groups; notes the parallel Hodaviah without silently changing the text.
verses.before: Jeshua with his sons and brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, stood together to oversee those doing the work in the house of God, along with the sons of Henadad and their sons and brothers, the Levites.
verses.after: Jeshua, his sons and relatives, and Kadmiel and his sons, descendants of Judah, stood together to oversee those working on God’s house. With them were the sons of Henadad, their sons, and their fellow Levites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jeshua with his sons and brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, stood together to oversee those doing the work in the house of God, along with the sons of Henadad and their sons and brothers, the Levites.

verses.rationale: Preserves the ceremonial clothing, instruments, and Davidic direction at the foundation ceremony.
verses.before: When the builders laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, the priests stood in their vestments with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the LORD according to the direction of David king of Israel.
verses.after: When the builders laid the foundation of the LORD’s temple, the priests took their places in their robes with trumpets, and the Levites descended from Asaph with cymbals, to praise the LORD as David king of Israel had directed.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the builders laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, the priests stood in their vestments with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the LORD according to the direction of David king of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the responsive form and recurring faithful-love wording, with the song inside the verse paragraph.
verses.before: They sang to one another in praise and thanksgiving to the LORD: “For he is good, for his steadfast love toward Israel endures forever.” And all the people gave a great shout of praise to the LORD because the foundation of the house of the LORD had been laid.
verses.after: They sang to one another in praise and thanksgiving to the LORD: “He is good; his faithful love for Israel lasts forever.” Then all the people raised a great shout of praise to the LORD because the foundation of his house had been laid.
verses.tsw_comparator: They sang to one another in praise and thanksgiving to the LORD: “For he is good, for his steadfast love toward Israel endures forever.” And all the people gave a great shout of praise to the LORD because the foundation of the house of the LORD had been laid.

verses.rationale: Preserves the older witnesses and simultaneous weeping and joy without assigning motives the verse does not state.
verses.before: But many of the priests, Levites, and heads of ancestral houses, old people who had seen the first house, wept with a loud voice when the foundation of this house was laid before their eyes, while many others raised their voices with a shout of joy.
verses.after: Many of the older priests, Levites, and family heads who had seen the first house wept aloud as they watched the foundation of this house being laid. Many others lifted their voices in joyful shouts.
verses.tsw_comparator: But many of the priests, Levites, and heads of ancestral houses, old people who had seen the first house, wept with a loud voice when the foundation of this house was laid before their eyes, while many others raised their voices with a shout of joy.

verses.rationale: Keeps the blended sounds and audible distance rather than resolving the mixed response.
verses.before: The people could not distinguish the sound of the shout of joy from the sound of the people’s weeping, for the people shouted with a great shout, and the sound was heard far away.
verses.after: No one could distinguish the joyful shouts from the people’s weeping. The people were shouting so loudly that the sound could be heard far away.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people could not distinguish the sound of the shout of joy from the sound of the people’s weeping, for the people shouted with a great shout, and the sound was heard far away.

verses.rationale: Retains the narrator’s characterization of the opponents and the returnees’ temple project.
verses.before: When the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the exile were building a temple to the LORD, the God of Israel,
verses.after: The enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the returned exiles were building a temple for the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the exile were building a temple to the LORD, the God of Israel,

verses.rationale: Follows the read to him instead of the written not and keeps the claim in the opponents’ own speech.
verses.before: they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of ancestral houses and said to them, “Let us build with you, for we seek your God as you do, and we have been sacrificing to him since the days of Esar-Haddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here.”
verses.after: They approached Zerubbabel and the family heads and said, “Let us build with you. We seek your God just as you do, and we have been sacrificing to him since Esarhaddon king of Assyria brought us here.”
verses.tsw_comparator: they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of ancestral houses and said to them, “Let us build with you, for we seek your God as you do, and we have been sacrificing to him since the days of Esar-Haddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here.”

verses.rationale: Makes the refusal explicit without adding an explanation of the opponents’ motives.
verses.before: Yet Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of ancestral houses of Israel said to them, “You have no part with us in building a house for our God. We ourselves together will build for the LORD, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus, king of Persia, commanded us.”
verses.after: But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the other family heads of Israel answered, “You have no part with us in building a house for our God. We ourselves will build for the LORD, the God of Israel, as Cyrus king of Persia commanded us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of ancestral houses of Israel said to them, “You have no part with us in building a house for our God. We ourselves together will build for the LORD, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus, king of Persia, commanded us.”

verses.rationale: Unfolds weakening hands and follows the read form frightened.
verses.before: Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah and frightened them from building.
verses.after: Then the people of the land discouraged the people of Judah and frightened them away from building.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah and frightened them from building.

verses.rationale: Preserves the organized interference and stated span across reigns.
verses.before: They hired counselors against them to frustrate their purpose all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
verses.after: They hired advisers against them to frustrate their plans throughout the reign of Cyrus king of Persia and until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
verses.tsw_comparator: They hired counselors against them to frustrate their purpose all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, until the reign of Darius king of Persia.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named reign without pretending the following material continues a simple chronological sequence.
verses.before: In the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.after: At the beginning of Ahasuerus’s reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Preserves the names and the double language/script description, with the language transition explained in a note.
verses.before: And in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of their associates wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia. The text of the document was written in Aramaic and translated in Aramaic.
verses.after: In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their other associates wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia. The letter was written in Aramaic script and expressed in Aramaic.
verses.tsw_comparator: And in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of their associates wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia. The text of the document was written in Aramaic and translated in Aramaic.

verses.rationale: Marks the new letter and preserves both official roles.
verses.before: Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes as follows.
verses.after: Rehum the commanding official and Shimshai the scribe wrote the following letter about Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes as follows.

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult group list and follows the read Dahae rather than collapsing it into the written relative phrase.
verses.before: Then Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates—the judges, officials, administrators, Persians, people of Erech, Babylonians, people of Susa, that is, Elamites,
verses.after: It came from Rehum the commanding official, Shimshai the scribe, and their other associates: the Dinaites, Apharsathchites, Tarpelites, Persians, people of Erech, Babylonians, people of Susa, Dahae, Elamites,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates—the judges, officials, administrators, Persians, people of Erech, Babylonians, people of Susa, that is, Elamites,

verses.rationale: Keeps deportation explicit, retains the ruler’s name as given, and preserves the formal transition.
verses.before: and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Osnappar deported and settled in the city of Samaria and in the rest of the province Beyond the River—and so forth.
verses.after: and the other peoples whom the great and honored Osnappar had deported and settled in the city of Samaria and elsewhere in Beyond the River. And now:
verses.tsw_comparator: and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Osnappar deported and settled in the city of Samaria and in the rest of the province Beyond the River—and so forth.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the narrator’s introduction from the document’s address.
verses.before: This is a copy of the letter that they sent to him: “To King Artaxerxes: Your servants, the people Beyond the River. And now:
verses.after: This is a copy of the letter they sent him: “To King Artaxerxes, from your servants, the men of Beyond the River. And now:
verses.tsw_comparator: This is a copy of the letter that they sent to him: “To King Artaxerxes: Your servants, the people Beyond the River. And now:

verses.rationale: Keeps the allegations inside the letter rather than presenting them as the translator’s judgment.
verses.before: Let it be known to the king that the Judeans who came up from you have come to us at Jerusalem. They are rebuilding the rebellious and evil city. They are finishing the walls and repairing the foundations.
verses.after: “Let the king know that the Jews who came up from you to us have reached Jerusalem. They are rebuilding that rebellious, wicked city, completing its walls and repairing its foundations.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let it be known to the king that the Judeans who came up from you have come to us at Jerusalem. They are rebuilding the rebellious and evil city. They are finishing the walls and repairing the foundations.

verses.rationale: Preserves the conditional warning and three revenue categories while noting uncertainty in the revenue phrase.
verses.before: Now let it be known to the king that if this city is rebuilt and the walls are finished, they will not pay tribute, tax, or toll, and in the end it will cause loss to the kings.
verses.after: Let the king also know that if this city is rebuilt and its walls completed, they will stop paying tribute, tax, and toll, and the royal revenue will suffer.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now let it be known to the king that if this city is rebuilt and the walls are finished, they will not pay tribute, tax, or toll, and in the end it will cause loss to the kings.

verses.rationale: Retains the ancient salt image and the writers’ stated loyalty rather than replacing the image with payroll language.
verses.before: Now because we eat the salt of the palace and it is not fitting for us to see the king dishonored, therefore we have sent and made this known to the king,
verses.after: We eat the palace’s salt, and it would not be right for us to watch the king be dishonored. That is why we are sending this report to the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now because we eat the salt of the palace and it is not fitting for us to see the king dishonored, therefore we have sent and made this known to the king,

verses.rationale: Preserves the appeal to records and the letter’s retrospective argument as its authors’ claim.
verses.before: so that a search may be made in the book of the records of your ancestors. You will find in the book of records and know that this city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, and that rebellion has been stirred up within it from ancient days. For this reason this city was destroyed.
verses.after: Have a search made in the records of your ancestors. There you will find that this city has been rebellious, harmful to kings and provinces, and a place of revolt from long ago. That is why the city was destroyed.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that a search may be made in the book of the records of your ancestors. You will find in the book of records and know that this city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, and that rebellion has been stirred up within it from ancient days. For this reason this city was destroyed.

verses.rationale: Keeps the strong territorial warning without moderating the writers’ rhetoric.
verses.before: We reveal to the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, you will have no possession in the province Beyond the River.”
verses.after: We inform the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls completed, you will have no territory left in Beyond the River.”
verses.tsw_comparator: We make known to the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, you will have no possession in the province Beyond the River.”

verses.rationale: Clearly marks the royal reply while retaining the full addressee and greeting.
verses.before: The king sent an answer: “To Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates who live in Samaria and elsewhere in the province Beyond the River: Peace. And now:
verses.after: The king sent this answer: “To Rehum the commanding official, Shimshai the scribe, and their other associates living in Samaria and elsewhere in Beyond the River: Peace. And now:
verses.tsw_comparator: The king sent an answer: “To Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates who live in Samaria and elsewhere in the province Beyond the River: Peace. And now:

verses.rationale: Retains the shift from royal us to my and the reading’s explanatory quality.
verses.before: The document that you sent to us has been read clearly before me.
verses.after: “The letter you sent us has been read and explained in my presence.
verses.tsw_comparator: The document that you sent to us has been read clearly before me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the reported finding and both terms for resistance.
verses.before: By my command a search was made, and it was found that this city has risen against kings from ancient days and that rebellion and revolt have been made in it.
verses.after: I ordered a search, and it was found that from long ago this city has risen against kings, and rebellion and revolt have taken place in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: By my command a search was made, and it was found that this city has risen against kings from ancient days and that rebellion and revolt have been made in it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the former kings’ power and the repeated three revenue categories.
verses.before: Powerful kings have ruled over Jerusalem and governed all the province Beyond the River, and tribute, tax, and toll were paid to them.
verses.after: Powerful kings have ruled Jerusalem and governed all Beyond the River. Tribute, tax, and toll were paid to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Powerful kings have ruled over Jerusalem and governed all the province Beyond the River, and tribute, tax, and toll were paid to them.

verses.rationale: Retains the city focus and the prohibition’s explicit endpoint.
verses.before: Now issue a command to make these men stop, so that this city is not rebuilt until a command is issued by me.
verses.after: Now issue an order to stop these men. This city must not be rebuilt until I give the order.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now issue a command to make these men stop, so that this city is not rebuilt until a command is issued by me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the warning and closing rhetorical question.
verses.before: Be careful not to neglect this. Why should damage increase to the injury of the kings?”
verses.after: Take care not to neglect this matter. Why should the damage grow and harm the royal interests?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Be careful not to neglect this. Why should damage increase to the injury of the kings?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the prompt response and the coercion expressed by arm and force.
verses.before: Then, when the copy of King Artaxerxes’ document was read before Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates, they went quickly to Jerusalem to the Judeans and made them stop by force and power.
verses.after: As soon as King Artaxerxes’s letter was read before Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates, they hurried to the Jews in Jerusalem and forcibly stopped them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then, when the copy of King Artaxerxes’ document was read before Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates, they went quickly to Jerusalem to the Judeans and made them stop by force and power.

verses.rationale: Signals the return to the temple narrative without changing the king or flattening the retrospective arrangement.
verses.before: Then the work on the house of God in Jerusalem stopped and remained stopped until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
verses.after: Work on God’s house in Jerusalem had come to a stop. It remained stopped until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the work on the house of God in Jerusalem stopped and remained stopped until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.

verses.rationale: Retains divine authority and the final over-them relation without merging it into the location.
verses.before: Now Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo, the prophets, prophesied to the Judeans who were in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel who was over them.
verses.after: The prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, who was over them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo, the prophets, prophesied to the Judeans who were in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel who was over them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two leaders and the prophets’ practical participation.
verses.before: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak arose and began to rebuild the house of God that is in Jerusalem, and the prophets of God were with them, supporting them.
verses.after: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak began rebuilding God’s house in Jerusalem. God’s prophets were there with them, supporting them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak arose and began to rebuild the house of God that is in Jerusalem, and the prophets of God were with them, supporting them.

verses.rationale: Retains the provincial title and authorization question; structure represents a difficult architectural term.
verses.before: At that time Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, and Shethar-Bozenai and their associates came to them and said this to them: “Who gave you a decree to build this house and complete this structure?”
verses.after: At that time Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates came to them and asked, “Who authorized you to build this house and complete this structure?”
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, and Shethar-Bozenai and their associates came to them and said this to them: “Who gave you a decree to build this house and complete this structure?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the pinned Aramaic first-person we rather than silently changing it to they; the narrative shift is noted.
verses.before: Then they also said to them, “What are the names of the men who are building this building?”
verses.after: Then we asked them, “What are the names of the men constructing this building?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they also said to them, “What are the names of the men who are building this building?”

verses.rationale: Retains the eye image and the continuing work during official inquiry.
verses.before: But the eye of their God was upon the elders of the Judeans, and they did not make them stop until a report could go to Darius and then a written answer be returned concerning it.
verses.after: But their God’s eye was on the Jewish elders. They were not stopped while a report went to Darius and a written reply about the matter was awaited.
